_note: Mate's source of truth for the fleet board. Update `stage` at every dispatch-loop transition. Granular stages (Kickoff, Build, Housekeeping, Squash, Testing, PR, Ready-for-Review, Ready-for-Testing, Merge, Merged) roll up on the board to the 8 canonical SDLC phases — Planning · Building · Housekeeping · Testing · Review · Validation · Merge · Shipped — rendered as a progress track (●●●◉○○○○). Note: dev's own unit/E2E = 'Testing'; third-party QA ('Ready for Testing') = 'Validation'; 'Merge' = green & mergeable (CI passing, no conflicts — captain's merge gate); 'Shipped' = merged. Rows are two-line: `jira` renders stacked under the ticket, and the optional `substep` field renders stacked under the phase — keep it to ONE terse token, never a sentence (a PR is just "draft #1196", or "#1196" once non-draft; a test is "E2E on burner"; no trailing prose). Keep `summary` <=24 chars (SUMMARY_W in bin/fleet) so it doesn't ellipsis-truncate and the board stays narrow enough (~77 cols) not to wrap an 80-col pane. `done` entries render their full `note` untruncated (they wrap) — keep the list short. There is no separate Jira column. Crew status is overlaid live from herdr by bin/fleet (joined on worktree path). Each item also carries a `name` — the crew member's handle (NATO phonetic: Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, …), the captain's way to refer to a crew member instead of a ticket #. Assign at dispatch = the lowest word not in use among in_flight (freed when the item retires); `bin/fleet --next-name` prints it. It renders as a prefix in the Crew cell. QA files bugs as Jira BUG SUBTASKS on the story a crew is working; the mate's `snd-qa-bugs` sweep records them in the item's optional `bugs` array — one object per bug: `key`, a short `summary`, `state` (open → dispatched → fixed; drop the entry once fixed and pushed), `triage` (auto|escalated), and `seen` (the timestamp that makes the sweep idempotent — a key already present is never re-announced). Outstanding bugs render as a `🐞 N` marker on the phase's continuation line, float the row just under the blocked ones, and list under 'QA bugs — open'. Two rules: open bugs do NOT set `blocked` (only a bug whose triage was escalated to the captain does, or every filing lights the board red), and a bug does NOT roll the phase back — the ticket really is at QA's gate, so it stays Validation and the bug count is what says it's bouncing. STATUS TRACK, drive it: bug subtask Open -> In Progress (crew working) -> Ready for Testing (fix pushed; QA closes it). Parent story sits In Progress while any bug is open, and MUST go back to Ready for Testing once the last one clears — QA is triggered to re-validate by the parent's status, so leaving it In Progress silently stalls the story. Keep `jira` honest against real Jira on every sweep; it is hand-maintained and drifts.
